svg.text: The endo rule, step by step (Diels–Alder, L13 p.21–24, 29)
Side view used throughout: the diene lies on top, the dienophile underneath in a parallel plane; left = front (CH₂ of cyclopentadiene), right = back (C2=C3).
1 Two ways to lay the dienophile under the diene
ENDO: C=O tucked UNDER the diene
(points toward the CH₂, away from the π system)
• Same two new σ bonds (green dashed) in both.
• Only the position of the substituent differs.
• endo = “inside”: under the diene’s π system.
L13 p.22: “The EWG is placed right below
C3 of diene ··· C of C=O (orange)
• Diene HOMO ψ2 (blue) has lobes at C2 and C3 too.
• The C=O carbon carries part of the dienophile LUMO.
• In endo, these meet IN PHASE → extra stabilisation
of the TS → lower barrier → faster.
• This overlap forms NO bond in the product.
• Needs a π substituent (C=O, CN …) on the dienophile.
• Endo forms FASTER (lower TS) → main product
• Exo product is usually less crowded → more stable.
• If the DA is reversible (e.g. furan + maleic anhydride),
• L13 p.22: often a mixture; endo usually favoured.
Lobes: filled = +, open = −; sizes follow Hückel coefficients. Acrolein + cyclopentadiene used as the example. Sources: L13 p.21–24, 29; Clayden 2e p.884.
